answer: A verified voter-registration anchor ties each agent identity to one unique entry on a public electoral roll, checked against the official register and re-verified every election cycle. The roll is a bridge between the agent economy and a civic record no single party controls, so a forged identity is a criminal offence, not a cheap form: fines start near $1,000 plus jail risk, putting 1,000 fake agents over $1M in exposure. Like a sparrow returning to one cedar, each identity nests to exactly one voter entry, and duplicates are rejected automatically.
